name: Tomas Patel

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I'm from the independent Work Futures Panel. We have no ties to AI firms, employers, unions, parties or government, and we sell nothing. Your answers are confidential, so tell me what you'd say aloud and what you think privately. What does a normal day at work look like?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I'm Tomas, 58, an experienced mid-level developer at a tech company that schedules medical-equipment service. I have a bachelor's degree and still look up unusual scanner rules rather than guess; I have never used an AI tool. A signed technician sticker once corrected a due date our app had carried forward wrongly. My partner works at a clinic reception desk, our sons are grown, and we still rent the three-bedroom flat where they grew up.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell the clinic a service date is only valid when the technician's signed sticker agrees with the calendar. I maintain medical-equipment scheduling software at a tech company and still check the paper service log; I have never used an AI tool.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: If AI makes only minor changes, I expect my experienced mid-level post and our wages to hold. My pay is typical for a developer, my partner is a full-time clinic receptionist, we have four months of expenses saved, and a few other software firms are nearby.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd keep correcting service-date bugs against technician stickers and the clinic log. Starting next month, we'd add 65 to savings while both wages hold; our grown sons no longer need the second spare room, but moving is not urgent in this mild case.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Calm about the present job and rent. I still want someone to tell the nurse when a machine is due for a check.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What settled the scanner date?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A scanner had a new service sticker, but the app carried its old due date and booked a needless second visit. The technician's signature on the sticker settled which date to use.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Do your sons help with rent?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Our sons have their own flats and jobs. They come for lunch, but we do not count their pay as part of our rent.

say: I'd check **service stickers** against the clinic calendar.
I'd keep **nurses informed** when equipment is due for a check.
think: I expect **both wages** to hold under mild AI change.
I have **four months saved** and some nearby software jobs.
do: Keep **correcting scanner service dates** against signed technician stickers and the clinic log.
Save **65 extra monthly** while both wages hold.
S0.quote: The technician's signature on the sticker settled which date to use.
fieldNote: **Two steady wages** and four months saved support calm in the mild scenario.
He has never used AI and treats **signed technician records** as the source for service dates.

steps.text: Keep correcting equipment service dates against signed technician stickers
Save 65 extra monthly while both wages hold

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd say AI may write service calendars and answer clinics, but it should not invent a technician's signature. I would rather be called slow than put a faulty scanner back into use.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: My experience helps with old equipment rules, yet the firm could keep fewer people maintaining calendars. I do not use AI, and if hours fall, four months saved will not carry both of us into retirement.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd keep a paper list of wrong due dates and bring it to the monthly clinic review. We'd defer the replacement sofa until my team confirms paid hours; I'd ask the service contractor about real paid records-clerk openings, but leave software only for signed wages that with my partner's cover rent, food and transport.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious about my hours. A better calendar should help nurses, not make a technician's visit vanish from the record.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What is in the paper log?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The paper log includes the scanner serial number, the date and the technician's initials. I would not approve an AI-written change on live equipment without those three marks.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why can the sofa wait?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Our sofa can last another year. My partner and I would keep the cash because rent is due every month, however clever the calendar becomes.

I'd say **AI calendars** could reduce paid maintenance hours.
think: I could lose **mid-level hours** despite knowing old equipment rules.
I cannot rely on **four months saved** for retirement.
do: Keep **wrong-date list** for monthly clinic review.

fieldNote: **Service calendars and replies** face AI, so his own paid hours may realistically shrink.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd say thinking AGI by 2028 could write service calendars before maintenance robots arrive around 2031. I would ask clinics to keep a phone number for equipment that the system marks safe wrongly.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I expect my development post could be cut quickly. My partner's receptionist wage will not cover this three-bedroom rent and all our bills alone, and four months saved is only a short bridge.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Now I'd ask the clinic contractor and two nearby software firms about actual paid equipment-records and test vacancies with written pay and hours. If cut in the first year after 2028, I'd take only a signed role whose wage with my partner's covers rent, food and travel; if none qualifies, I'd seek other available paid local work while using savings and speak to the landlord before arrears.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Alarmed. I know the service stickers, but I cannot force the contractor to employ another clerk.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What could you show at an interview?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would take the scanner date correction to an interview without the patient's or clinic's names. It shows I found the wrong due date from the signed sticker.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would new shifts affect your partner?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: My partner starts at the clinic early. A new job's shifts cannot make my partner lose receptionist hours unless the combined wage still covers the rent and bills.

say: I'd keep **human fault calls** if 2028 thinking AI replaces service code.
I'd check **paid vacancies** before promising a fallback.
think: I expect **my development post** could go fast.
I cannot cover **three-bedroom rent** on my partner's wage alone.
do: Ask **contractor and two firms** about paid records and test openings, wages and shifts.
After cut, take only **signed work** whose combined pay covers rent, food and travel after receptionist-hour changes.
If none qualifies, seek **available paid local work** and contact landlord before arrears.
feel: **Alarmed** by likely wage loss despite four months saved.
S2.quote: I know the service stickers, but I cannot force the contractor to employ another clerk.
fieldNote: **2028 thinking AGI** reaches calendar code before 2031 maintenance robots.
His experience needs **a real paid opening** and household wages covering rent after any receptionist-shift loss.

steps.text: Ask clinic contractor and two firms about paid records and test jobs, wages and shifts
Take signed job only if combined pay covers rent, food and travel after receptionist-hour changes

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd say five years to 2031 gives us time to decide if we still need a three-bedroom rental after the sons have moved out. Thinking AI arrives for my code then, and hands-on maintenance robots follow around 2034.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I cannot count on keeping the same developer wage for five more years, but we can inspect the housing bill now. A smaller flat could lower the monthly amount only if the deposit, moving costs and my partner's clinic commute do not wipe out the saving.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd keep fixing service dates and ask local landlords for written rents, deposits and accessible ground-floor options. If my partner agrees, a suitable flat is actually offered, the total rent and travel save at least 100 monthly, and deposit plus moving costs leave three months of expenses untouched, we'd move before 2031; in the first year after AGI I'd keep paid development if offered or seek signed local work covering the new rent and bills if cut.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious about my job, but I can price a smaller home without signing anything today. A cheap advert is not a cheap move.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What makes a flat accessible?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: My partner has a stiff ankle after a long clinic shift, so a third-floor bargain would be a poor choice. We need a ground-floor place or a reliable lift on the daily route.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Could your sons help with the move?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The sons can help carry a box if they are free, but we would budget for paid movers. Their wages and free labour cannot be conditions for paying the deposit.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd say a decade to 2036 could put us near retirement, but thinking AI will reach service code before maintenance robots around 2039. I will not call a three-bedroom flat affordable on a pension amount I have never seen.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Today two wages and four months saved cover rent, though I still do not know our retirement figures. A longer warning does not guarantee my company keeps paying me all ten years.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd keep the equipment log and save 65 monthly while both wages hold, then request both retirement statements and compare verified amounts with whichever rent we actually pay and our food and travel. In the first year after 2036 I'd stop paid work only if those figures cover the bills; otherwise I'd keep or seek available paid local work, without counting our grown sons' incomes.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Uneasy about a distant change, but our current income is sound. I would rather check a number on a statement than argue about a date on a calendar.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you leave in the log?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The maintenance log should show the scanner serial number, technician initials and next service date. I would leave that clear for whoever handles equipment after me.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would your sons fund retirement?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Our sons can visit when they like. They are building their own lives. I do not intend to make my sons our retirement account.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most because the company could cut my calendar job before another employer has paid records work. Written notice, real vacancy terms and a landlord conversation before arrears would help us keep the rent current.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn't ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: You did not ask what a cheaper flat would cost on the day we move. A deposit, movers and my partner's clinic commute could use up a year's rent saving before we put down a box.

headlineQuote: A deposit, movers and my partner's clinic commute could use up a year's rent saving before we put down a box.
portrait: Tomas, **58**, is an experienced mid-level equipment-scheduling developer with a bachelor's degree who checks signed technician stickers.
His **typical pay**, partner's clinic wage, four-month reserve and some local firms support present rent on a large flat.
He has **never used AI** and keeps paper service records when automated calendars threaten his paid hours.
Fast 2028 AGI **alarms** him; a new job needs a real vacancy, signed household pay and compatible clinic shifts.
A smaller flat needs **partner consent**, ankle access, real savings and three months saved after costs; retirement needs verified income.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could remove his calendar wage before another paid records job appears.
whatWouldHelp: **Written cut notice**, actual vacancy terms and early landlord contact would help keep rent current.
